newsitem.title: MEXICO: GMexico share spike piques curiousity.
newsitem.headline: GMexico share spike piques curiousity.

text.p: Grupo Mexico (GMexico) shares have spiked in recent sessions on the back of a cocktail of pending business ventures for Mexico's largest mining company and healthier copper prices, analysts say.
Falling world copper inventories have boosted prices of the base metal from the doldrums and fallout of the summer Sumitomo scandal, and GMexico has reaped the rewards.

"Since falling to an 18-month low of 21.70 pesos per share at the end of October, GMexico has bounced back, driven by tightness in the world copper market," Valores Finamex analyst Christopher Albi said in a report.
GMexico is currently trading in a tight range around 25.50 to 26 pesos per share.
But analysts also point to business ventures in the pipeline for GMexico that are spurring interest in the normally cyclical, copper-price-driven equity play.
"Their heading a bid in the railway privatization is causing market interest," ING Baring mining analyst Sebastian Barry-Taylor said. GMexico leads a consortium called Grupo Ferroviario Mexicano.

The line is the jewel in the crown of the Mexican railroad system up for sale from the government. It includes the prime lines of Mexico City-Nuevo Laredo, Mexico City-Veracruz and Mexico City-Lazaro Cardenas.
Bids could be as high as $1 billion. The government is scheduled to open the bids from the five groups interested in the network and announce the winners on Dec 5.
"Although this railroad has no synergies with GMexico's mining operations, the market seems to be taking the company's bid as serious," Barry-Taylor said.
But other railways coming on the block in future privatizations would have greater direct interest for GMexico because of their proximity to the company's Sonoran mines, he added.

Another pending business decision awaited by markets is the outcome of GMexico's El Arco copper-gold mine final study, which is expected at any time. The study is looking at deposits in a field in Baja California state.

In a recent interview, GMexico finance director Carlos Oyanguren said the outcome of the study would dictate the future of the deposit, hinting that investments could be in a range of $200 million to $1 billion. But analysts are sure GMexico is waiting for the government's Northeast Railroad decision before making the study available and also waiting for a better fix on the long-term trend of copper prices before commiting to developing El Arco.
"They are bound to be taking an allocation of resources type view of the two projects (railroad and El Arco)," said one analyst who asked to remain anonymous.
GMexico spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.
